A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dynamic Token Morphing in the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and relocated experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original pilot experiments, ImageNet classification, ADE20K segmentation, transfer-learning results and DTM ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds an EVA-CLIP token-aggregation analysis with ImageNetV2 zero-shot results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The overall DTM scheduler, matching procedure and cosine objective are retained. However, v4 defines M using normalized intermediate matrices while still calling M binary and interpreting its row sums as token-count loss weights. This leaves an unresolved distinction between changed weighting and inconsistent additional documentation. The unmasked target input specified in v4 was already depicted in v3 Figure 4.

E1.justification: v4 adds ImageNetV2 zero-shot evaluation in Appendix A. The existing ImageNet-1K/100, ADE20K, iNaturalist and fine-grained classification coverage remains; moving applicability experiments to the appendix does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds reported comparisons with AdPE and MI-MAE while retaining the earlier comparators. The reordered pilot comparisons and relocated SLIP and SSL-framework tables preserve their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A evaluation uses EVA-01-CLIP-g/14, aggregates 128 of its 256 tokens and compares globally pooled token-wise zero-shot predictions with and without aggregation. This adds a model configuration and evaluation setting; the retained experiments' training budgets, metrics and hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a qualitative example and quantitative analysis testing whether spatial inconsistency persists in a stronger, larger EVA-CLIP teacher. Existing analyses of scheduling, randomness, normalization, loss functions, clustering and convergence are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report best accuracy and mean plus standard deviation across hyperparameter-grid configurations for transfer learning: v3 Tables A–B become v4 Tables C–D. There are no added seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds EVA-CLIP ImageNetV2 accuracies of 51.2% without aggregation and 53.1% with aggregation, plus AdPE and MI-MAE result rows. Table 3 revises the SplistMask segmentation entry from 46.8 to 45.7. DTM's principal classification scores, 83.2/85.4/86.7%, and segmentation score, 53.1, remain unchanged, as do the retained transfer and ablation results.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a recursive matrix construction, changes Equation (3) from sums to normalized averages, and changes the stated total sum of M entries from N to n-bar. These are formal revisions without new theorems or proofs. The normalized construction conflicts with the retained binary-matrix and column-sum statements.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the explicit faster-training assertion with improved training trends evidenced by lower losses and qualifies the reduction of spatial inconsistency. The central contributions concerning DTM, low overhead, benchmark superiority and transferability remain.

C2.justification: v4 treats pilot accuracy improvements and convergence evidence more cautiously, using suggestive rather than definitive interpretations. It elaborates information loss from early layer-wise token reduction and interprets the EVA-CLIP analysis as extending the inconsistency concern to stronger teachers. The limitation on training DTM beyond ViT-L/16 remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds Algorithm 1 and detailed iterative matching documentation, and explicitly identifies the pilot's CLIP-B/16 teacher. Conversely, it removes v3's sentence specifying L=2, sampling lower bounds 1 and 147, and K=14. The ablations still identify two schedules and K=14, but do not restore both sampling bounds. The code-access statement and general training recipes remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for EVA-CLIP, EVA-02, ImageNetV2, AdPE and MI-MAE. The basic positioning against efficiency-oriented token aggregation is retained. Publication, title and venue updates for existing references do not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, pilot-study narrative, method explanation and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. The experimental narrative is reorganized, SLIP and SSL-framework discussions move to the appendix, and appendix sections are regrouped around the algorithm, applicability and empirical studies.

P2.justification: v4 adds the matrix-construction schematic in Figure 5, the EVA-CLIP visualization in Appendix Figure A and an algorithm display. It revises the overview diagram, reorders Tables 2–3 and moves the SLIP and SSL-framework tables into the appendix. The existing learning curves and CLIP example images are reused.

improvement.justification: The EVA-CLIP analysis, expanded comparisons, more cautious claims and additional explanations provide benefits. However, the new normalized-matrix construction conflicts with retained definitions and loss weights, while removal of the sampling bounds weakens reproducibility. With the principal empirical results unchanged, these competing effects do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
